blurb: A sqlite Store is created and removed; a PostgreSQL database is connected and disconnected with its URL and login, saved on this computer only, and machines attach to it to run its Sandboxes. Default reads use the home's records.
reasons: Why engine: type means file, dir or symlink everywhere else.
Why rows list projects: a project count needs a name for the number; the short list of names answers both.
Why secrets come on stdin: a password in an argument lands in shell history and process listings.
Why connect is not create: LayerFS makes and deletes a sqlite file; a PostgreSQL database exists outside LayerFS and stays when it is disconnected.
Why a saved login without an address: the address is the part that differs per machine and per proxy; the login is the part that is the same everywhere.
Why the auth calls live in store: a top-level layerfs auth would read like logging in to LayerFS itself.
Why move names the destination: push and pull were one operation with two names. store move shop dev sends it; store move shop native brings it back.
Why no default machine on a PostgreSQL Store: no machine owns it. Where a Sandbox runs is chosen at sandbox create.

calls.new_work: A records-only state is new: today each item's state comes from the leases and a `stat` on the Store's machine, and is idle, in_use, busy, down or unresolved. `--machine` is a new filter. `blocked` with `blocked_by` replaces `down`.

calls.note: + store.status, store.stats. state comes from the home's records, with no probe. A sqlite Store is ready, blocked with blocked_by {machine, reason} when its machine is not ready, busy with op {name, phase, started_at} (name is move, remove, compact, backup or restore), or broken with reason and fix. A PostgreSQL Store is ready, busy or broken; it waits on no machine. unresolved is an operation whose outcome is not known and whose owner is gone; its fix is the call that clears it: the same layerfs store move <store> <machine> for a move, layerfs store remove <store> for a remove, layerfs store compact <store> for a compaction (the next run adopts and settles what the earlier one left), and layerfs store get <store> --with live for a backup or a restore. A live read is what first sees missing (no file where the record says; the fix restores a backup or removes the Store) and unreachable (this computer cannot reach the PostgreSQL server; the fix is layerfs store doctor <store>); it writes the record only when the state word or its reason changes, and from then on a records-only read answers them too. unknown with observed_at is answered only by the live read that could not be made, and is never recorded. observed_at is kept beside the record, in an observation file the home's generation does not cover; a write of the record moves generation. An op whose owner is gone and whose outcome is certain is ignored on read, with no write. A sqlite Store answers machine; a PostgreSQL Store answers auth and connections (the one without a machine is the one every machine uses) and has no default machine. The other engine's keys are null in the long form. projects shows the first 20 names. Each backups row is {bucket}, and in the long form {bucket, file, sha256, heads_sha256, last, attempt}: last is the last transfer that worked ({call, ended_at, size}), attempt one that did not ({call, ended_at, error}, else null); last_transfer is {call, from, to, ended_at, size, sha256, heads_sha256, retired}. heads_sha256 was heads. With --with live a sqlite Store on another machine is read through that machine, the compaction record beside its file included: a run live there reads busy (op compact with its phase), even when this home's record holds that run unresolved after a lost reply; while the machine is stopped the Store reads blocked and nothing is asked of it. Whether a machine reaches a PostgreSQL Store is the doctor's to say (store doctor), not this call's. live.phases lists the steps the compaction record can show, in order: on SQLite mark, build, verify, install, cleanup (the record writes cleanup in its final step); store compact's progress events stay mark, build, verify, install (V19-12). connections (spec v23) lists every side that connects to a PostgreSQL Store's database: this computer first (machine null, the Store's address), then by name each machine with an address of its own, a reach seen from it, or a Sandbox of the Store; native without an address of its own is this computer's row. A row is {url} with machine and reached (ok or failed; absent when nothing was seen) in the short form, and {machine, url, own, server, reached, reach} in the long: own is whether the URL is the machine's own, server the {host, port, database} it names, reach the last reach seen {at, ok, latency_ms, server_version, error} or null. A reach is written to the Store's observation file by store connect --machine, every store doctor reach and each Sandbox made on a machine; it moves no generation. binding (long form) is the first 8 bytes of the id in the Store's schema as 16 hex: one database behind two addresses has one binding. A PostgreSQL Store whose record holds what 2.0 no longer writes (a password, a URL with a user or a login parameter, a machines.<m> entry with anything but its url) is broken outdated with fix: layerfs store update <store> --auth <auth>, which writes it clean; one naming a login the home does not hold is broken missing with fix: layerfs store save-auth <auth> --user <user> --password-stdin && layerfs store update <store> --auth <auth>, which wins over outdated. Neither refuses a call.

live.help: reads the Store where it lives, starting nothing: a sqlite Store's file through its machine, a PostgreSQL Store's server from this computer; state, its companion and observed_at at the top level then come from the read, and the record is written only when the state word or its reason changed. It settles an uncertain backup or restore whose owner is gone. holders: the pids of other live processes that hold it; phases: the steps a running compaction's record can show, in order (SQLite mark, build, verify, install, cleanup; the record writes cleanup in its final step), else null; behind: the buckets whose backup is older than the Store, null for PostgreSQL; server_version and latency_ms: the PostgreSQL server's answer, null for sqlite

stats.help: opens the Store where it lives. size: the file with its write-ahead log (sqlite), the schema (PostgreSQL); logical_bytes, canonical_bytes, stored_bytes, metadata_bytes: the Store's publication counters; file_bytes: the database's pages; reusable_bytes: reusable pages, null for PostgreSQL; dedupe and compression: ratios as text, six decimals; init: {entries, files, size, canonical_bytes, stored_bytes, metadata_bytes, duration_ms} of the first project init, or null

calls.new_work: Records-only state with the six states is new: today store.get answers no state and store.status always reads the leases, the file or the server. So that every client sees `busy`, store.compact, backup.create and backup.restore must record an `op` in the Store's record; today only a move and a remove do (a compaction keeps its own record beside the Store, backup.create holds a file lock). `live.behind` is new: it reads the Store's heads where it lives, through its worker on a machine (today backup.list compares them on native only). `attempt` on a backup row is new: today a link is written only after a transfer succeeds. `auth` and `connections` are new (see store.save_auth, store.connect). The reason codes `missing` and `unreachable` replace today's `down_reason` sentence. A live read writing the record when the state word or reason changes, and the observation file for `observed_at`, are new (today a read writes nothing). Clearing an uncertain operation: a move by the same move or `store remove`, a remove by `store remove`, and a compaction by the next `store compact` all exist today (store.status names the clearing call). A backup and a restore record no `op` today, so nothing needs clearing; once they record one, `store get --with live` settling an uncertain backup or restore whose owner is gone is new work: a backup changes nothing in the Store and a restore installs by one rename, so the read sees which file is there, drops the `op` and writes what was tried to the link's `attempt`. v19: a live read lets a compaction live on the Store's machine win over this home's `unresolved` record of it (after a lost reply), and answers `blocked` before any read while the machine is stopped. v23: `connections` rows list every side that connects (own address, a reach seen, a Sandbox), each with `reached` and the long `own`, `server`, `reach`; reaches are kept in the Store's observation file; `binding` is new in the long form; old record fields read `outdated` and a missing login `missing`.

calls.note: PostgreSQL. The URL holds host, port, database and TLS options; one with a user or a password is refused InvalidInput. First connect: --auth is required, here and only here; it is made from this computer, which gives an empty database the LayerFS schema and its id, or reads them, and answers the projects found. The URL is the address every machine uses. On a connected Store: with --machine the URL becomes that machine's own address, proven from that machine; without it, it replaces the address every machine uses, proven from this computer. Either must read the Store's id (Unavailable otherwise) and refuses --auth and --synchronous-commit (InvalidInput: a machine never has its own login; both change with store update). A Store has at most one address for every machine and one per machine. A database whose id another Store of this home holds is Exists. projects shows the first 20 names. A running Sandbox keeps its route Its connections are store get's rows (spec v23). --machine records the machine's check as its reach. A URL naming a user or carrying a login parameter (user, any password, passfile) is refused InvalidInput with a fix that gives the address alone: on a first connect after store save-auth, naming that login with --auth; on a connected Store (no --auth on connect) after store update --auth, with --machine for a machine's own address (spec v23 V23-13, LF11); sslkey and sslcert name files and pass. Every PostgreSQL record write drops the fields 2.0 no longer writes.

calls.note: freed_bytes is how much the Store's file or database shrank; on SQLite it can exceed the total of the wholly dead packs, since a rebuild also drops the dead records inside the packs it keeps. The long form is today's report with byte totals named _bytes: discarded_bytes (logical_discarded), reusable_bytes (backend_reusable), dead_bytes (bound and refined are equal; on SQLite it includes the dead records inside packs the run keeps), generation_before and generation_after, residue_*; kept_waste is {dead_in_retained_packs_bytes, delta_bases_bytes, inode_blocks_bytes}, and on a SQLite compacted run it describes the rebuilt Store. outcome is compacted or unchanged (today's path rebuild or none); on SQLite unchanged means dead_bytes is under 10% of the Store. delta_base_references shows its first 20 ids: today up to 1024, about 69 KB. Phases: mark, build, verify, install (sqlite; an unchanged run sends mark only); mark, build, swap, cleanup (PostgreSQL). A sqlite Store on another machine is compacted by that machine's worker, which sends the same phases; it starts no machine. The run is the Store's op (compact) while it runs. A run whose reply is lost, or that left a residue, leaves its own record beside the Store and the Store reads broken, unresolved; the next store compact adopts and settles it, as today. Refusals: Unavailable when the machine is stopped, records no worker or its worker does not answer (fix layerfs machine start M), or its worker is of another build (fix layerfs machine stop M && layerfs machine start M, --force on the stop when Sandboxes are on it); Busy while a machine operation holds the machine, or a compaction runs (here or in the worker), with op; Unknown when the reply is lost after the request went out (fix layerfs store compact <store>); InUse while Workspaces are mounted; Unresolved when an earlier run left its outcome unknown (fix layerfs store compact <store>)

calls.note: the Store, by the checks of checks.store in order, then a shallow check of each project (project doctor's list: project.record, project.listed; a project on record that the Store does not list is a notice with a fix, not an error). The same Store list runs wherever a Store is checked, by home doctor and machine doctor too. It stops after the schema check and reads no data: project doctor --full reads data. A PostgreSQL Store is also probed from each machine that has a Sandbox of it (R9): one store.connection check per machine, with from naming the machine, on the check entry and on its finding. --machine adds a probe from one more machine, Sandbox or not; it is for the command line and is refused InvalidInput for a sqlite Store. store.backups reports a backup that is behind as a notice on the Store, one finding per bucket, naming the bucket in message and fix (layerfs backup create <store> <bucket>); it is left out for a PostgreSQL Store and for a Store with no bucket link. store.operation reads the home's record and, for a sqlite Store, the compaction record beside its file through its machine (a run live there passes; one left there is an error with fix layerfs store compact <store>). Under a stopped machine store.record is made and the rest, store.operation included, are not_checked with blocked_by. The tree is the Store's node with projects. Today's ids: store.worker and the store.connection.* steps fold into store.connection (the failing step is in the finding's evidence), store.snapshot into store.schema; store.connection.kind is dropped (one doctor serves both engines); store.integrity.*, store.database.*, store.catalog.*, store.history.*, store.namespace, store.packs, store.objects, store.ordinal_blocks, store.acquisition.*, store.merge.* and store.advisory.* are dropped with the whole-Store scan. Exits 0 once the report is made A PostgreSQL Store is dialled from this computer, then from every machine with an address of its own, a Sandbox of it, or --machine; every reach, this computer's included (with its latency and server version), is written to the Store's observation file and read back as store get's connections (spec v23).

calls.new_work: The call is new on the table. The shallow Store check is new work (C14): today's cheapest Store mode still scans the file, so it needs a cut that stops after the schema check and a new argument on the worker's Store diagnosis that an older worker will not know. Probing a PostgreSQL Store from each machine that has a Sandbox of it is new; the probe itself exists (store.status --machine uses it). `store.operation` and `store.backups` are new check ids: the first reads the record's `op` and the leases, the second reads the Store's heads where it lives (the same read as store.get --with live `behind`) and compares them with each link. `store.record`, `store.identity`, `store.connection` and `store.schema` exist. The project record comparison exists (project.get makes it); reporting it as a notice is new. One answer shape, a time budget per thing and one progress event per finished thing ({phase: self|projects, done, total, node}) are new. v19: `store.operation` also reads a sqlite Store's compaction record through its machine (the shallow cut answers it), and is `not_checked` with `blocked_by` under a stopped machine.
